newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Premiere makes block buster debut.
newsitem.headline: Premiere makes block buster debut.

text.p: Premiere Entertainment Productions Inc got a rousing welcome on its debut at the Philippine Stock Exchange on Monday but analysts said the issue remained a speculative buy.
Shares of Premiere soared by 26 percent, ending at 1.26 pesos (4.8 cents) against its offering price of one peso.
Brokers said the issue had reached a high of 1.30 pesos in the grey market soon after the initial public offering was launched on April 2.
Premiere, the first Philippine movie producer to go public, sold 180 million common shares representing 34.62 percent of its outstanding capital stock.

"It was a block buster listing. It came at the right time, just when investors were ready to take a second look at Manila stocks after last week's battering" said Henry Ong, research director at Sapphire Securities.
But analysts said earnings prospects of the company remained speculative.
Premiere has projected a net income 17.388 million pesos this year against a net loss of 14.418 million pesos last year.

"The company has the funkiest disclosure in the market since they tell you what movies are coming, including the actors and actresses. But how will you know if these movies would click at the tills?," said one foreign broker who requested not to be named.

Julie Villena, analyst at Magnum Securities Inc, said Premier Entertainment was now fully valued at 1.26 pesos. The issue was offered at 20 times its price-earnings ratio for 1997 against the market's 16 times, she said.

"With so many barriers the film-making industry is facing, uncertainties continue to pose a major problem. The forecasts made by the company face a high margin of error due to its speculative nature," Villena said.
But Premiere president Cirilo Santiago said prospects were bright as proceeds of the IPO would enable production of more films as well as fund a diversification programme.

"With limited capital you can't go global," he said. Last year, only 11 percent of local films produced made money because of high competition with foreign films and rampant film piracy in the country, Santiago said. High taxes on the production of local films also weigh down revenues, he said.
Premiere has earmarked 560 million pesos this year to produce at least 12 films, four of which will be for export.
Some of the money will also be used to buy new equipment and for diversification into cinema houses and a television station.
"We are negotiating for an equity in Channel 35 and we are planning to bid in the privatisation of Channel 9 and 13 soon," he said.

Premiere already has an equity in local television Channel 21, through its affiliate Gem Communications Inc. It was also negotiating with Viva Films, one of the country's largest film producers, for a joint venture on cable TV production.
The company is also wooing foreign film producers, among them U.S.-based Orion Pictures Corp, to be its exclusive distributor in the Philippines.
